questions.question: You want a compact history: one line per commit with its short hash and subject. Which command?
questions.explanation: `--oneline` is short for `--pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit`. Add `-n 10` (or just `-10`) to limit the number of commits. `-p` shows each commit's full diff, and `--stat` lists the changed files.

questions.question: You want to see how all branches split off and merged, as a picture in the terminal. Which command?
questions.explanation: `--graph` draws the commit graph with ASCII lines, and `--all` includes every branch and tag instead of only the current branch. This is worth an alias: `git config --global alias.lg 'log --oneline --graph --all'`.

questions.question: You want the history of `src/billing.py`, including the commits from before it was renamed from `src/invoice.py`. Which command?
questions.explanation: `git log -- <path>` only shows commits that touched that exact path. `--follow` continues past renames. The `--` separates options and revisions from paths, which avoids confusion when a file has the same name as a branch.

questions.question: Somebody added, and later removed, the string `API_KEY` somewhere in the code. Which command finds the commits that added or removed it?
questions.explanation: `-S` (the "pickaxe") lists commits where the number of occurrences of the string changed, which means it was added or removed. Add `-p` to see the diffs. `--grep` searches commit **messages**, and `git grep` searches the current files.

questions.question: Which command lists the commits whose **message** mentions "invoice"?
questions.explanation: `--grep` filters on the commit message. Add `-i` for a case-insensitive search. It combines with other filters such as `--author` and `--since`.

questions.question: For a standup you want your own commits from the last week. Which command?
questions.explanation: `--author` matches part of the author name or email, and `--since` / `--until` accept dates like `2026-11-01` or phrases like `'2 weeks ago'`. `-n 7` limits the output to 7 commits, not 7 days.

questions.question: Line 42 of `config.py` has a strange value. Which command tells you who last changed that line, and in which commit?
questions.explanation: `git blame` prints the commit, author and date of the last change for each line; `-L start,end` limits it to a range. Then use `git show <hash>` to see the whole commit and its message. `git log -L 42,42:config.py` exists too: it shows every commit that changed those lines.

questions.question: A colleague mentions commit `a1b2c3d`. Which command shows its message and the changes it made?
questions.explanation: `git show` prints the commit's metadata and its diff against its parent. `git log a1b2c3d` would list that commit **and all its ancestors**, and `git diff a1b2c3d` compares that commit with your current working tree.

questions.question: You want to read `src/app.js` as it was three commits ago, without changing your working tree. Which command?
questions.explanation: The `<revision>:<path>` syntax names a file inside a commit; `git show` prints it. Redirect it to save a copy: `git show HEAD~3:src/app.js > old_app.js`. `git restore --source` would overwrite your working copy.

questions.question: What does `git diff` without arguments compare?
options: The working tree with the staging area: changes you haven't staged
The staging area with the last commit
The working tree with the last commit
questions.explanation: So after `git add`, those changes disappear from `git diff`. Use `git diff --staged` for staged changes, and `git diff HEAD` for both together.

questions.question: Which commits does this list?
options: Commits on `feature` that are not on `main`
Commits on `main` that are not on `feature`
Commits on either branch but not on both
All commits made between the dates of `main` and `feature`
questions.explanation: `A..B` means "reachable from B but not from A": what `feature` would add if merged into `main`. Swap them (`feature..main`) to see what's new on `main`. `git log origin/main..main` shows the commits you haven't pushed yet.

questions.question: `main` and `feature` have both moved on since `feature` branched off. You want to see only the changes made **on `feature`**, the way a pull request shows them. Which command?
questions.explanation: With `git diff`, three dots compare `feature` with the **merge base** (the commit where it branched off), so new commits on `main` don't show up as "removed" lines. `main..feature` in `git diff` just compares the two tips directly. Note that dots mean something different in `git log`.

questions.question: You want an overview of which files changed and how many lines, without the full diff. Which command?
questions.explanation: `--stat` prints one line per file with a +/- bar and a summary line. `--name-only` gives just the file names, and `--name-status` adds a letter (A added, M modified, D deleted, R renamed). These options work for `git show` and `git log` too.

questions.question: Which command counts commits per author, sorted from most to fewest?
questions.explanation: `git shortlog` groups commits by author; `-s` shows only the counts and `-n` sorts by count. Add `--since='1 month ago'` or a range such as `v1.0..v2.0` to narrow it down.
